title: Which Coin Was Chosen?
problem: Choose one of two coins uniformly. Coin A lands heads with probability 3/4; Coin B is fair. The chosen coin produces H,H,H,T. What is the probability Coin A was chosen?

hints.text: Compare the likelihood of the exact sequence under each coin.
The likelihoods are (3/4)^3(1/4) and (1/2)^4; equal priors make the posterior their normalized ratio.

solution.setup: Let D be the observed ordered sequence HHHT. The prior odds are 1:1.
solution.sanityCheck: Three heads favor A, while the tail prevents overwhelming evidence; the posterior around 0.628 is reasonably above one-half.

keyInsight: Posterior odds equal prior odds multiplied by the likelihood ratio.
recognitionCues: Competing data-generating models and an observed sample call for likelihood comparison.
commonMistakes: Ignoring the final tail when computing Coin A's likelihood.
followUps: How would the posterior change after HHHH?
